United States would be exceptional among major nations in being 
constitutionally barred from having an independent central bank. The 
relative pohtical independence of whatever government agency has power 
to affect the money supply (and thus the price of money to borrowers) is 
often thought critical to relative price stability and long-term economic 
growth.
In addition, common understanding within government as to whether 
presidents may fire all officers at will or are dependent for their removal 
authority on congressional authority may affect the organizational 
psychology of the executive branch as a whole. One of us has written that 
the theory of comprehensive presidential removal power is part and parcel 
of a too-unilateralist understanding of executive authority that creates an 
ethos of presidential entitlement which works against the rule of law. 
Within the executive branch, it may be that a prevailing “|I]egal awareness 
that executive authority [including removal authority] is significantly at 
the sufferance of Congress should lead a President to act with greater 
prudence and integrity.” PETER M. SHANE, MADISON’S NIGHTMARE: HOW 
Ex e c u t iv e Po w e r  Th r e a t e n s  Ame r ic a n  De mo c r a c y  185 (2009).
In reading materials about ‘‘independent agencies,” it should be noted 
that the phrase may be used in different ways. The United States 
Government Manual, for example, uses “independent establishment” or 
“independent agency” to mean only that an administrative establishment 
is not located within a larger agency. For this reason, as its web site will 
teU you, even the Central Intelligence Agency may be called an 
“independent agency,” although it is nothing like a regulatory commission 
in either its mission or organization, and it most certainly bears direct 
pohcy accountability to the president. Congress has on one occasion 
itemized the agencies it considers to be “independent regulatory 
commissions.” Paperwork Reduction Act of 1980, 44 U.S.C. § 3502(10). The 
operational consequence of being labeled “independent” in section 3502(10) 
is that an agency is not bound, under the Paperwork Reduction Act, by 
0MB disapproval of its use of particular methods for the collection of 
information from private parties. 44 U.S.C. § 3507(c). The statute does not 
indicate, however, any other way in which the agency is to be deemed 
exempt from the president’s direct policy influence. In any event. 
Congress’s use of the label “independent” presumably cannot be conclusive 
as to aU questions regarding the president’s relationship with that agency. 
If that were so. Congress could limit the president’s control over 
constitutionally based powers that he exercises personally by purporting to 
lodge such powers with an agency and denominating it “independent.”
